paper_title: High Efficiency over 18.6% of Organic Solar Cells Enabled by PEDOT:PSS/Br-2PACz Dual-Anode Interface

knowledge_points.content: The organic solar cell utilizing a PEDOT:PSS/Br-2PACz dual-anode interface achieved a peak power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 18.61%, with a short-circuit current (Jsc) of 27.84 mA cm⁻² and a fill factor (FF) of 78.17%.
knowledge_points.evidence: As a result, the Jsc and FF of the device are significantly improved, and the highest efficiency is up to 18.61%, which is obviously higher than that of pure Br-2PACz (16.58%) and PEDOT:PSS (17.64%) anode interface.

knowledge_points.content: The device architecture consists of a conventional structure: ITO/PEDOT:PSS/Br-2PACz/PBDBTCl-DTBT:BTP-4F/PDINN/Ag.
knowledge_points.evidence: Organic solar cells were fabricated on ITO glass substrates with an ITO/PEDOT:PSS/active layer/PDINN/Ag conventional structure... where the HTL is a dual-anode interface composed of PEDOT:PSS and Br-2PACz.

knowledge_points.content: The optimal concentration of the Br-2PACz solution used to modify the PEDOT:PSS layer is 0.1 mg/mL in ethanol, with higher or lower concentrations leading to a decrease in Jsc and FF.
knowledge_points.evidence: The results show that the device performs best when the Br-2PACz concentration is 0.1 mg/mL, but Jsc and FF decrease significantly with a further increase or decrease of the concentration.

knowledge_points.content: The conductivity of the PEDOT:PSS/Br-2PACz dual-layer film is 6.29 × 10⁻⁴ S m⁻¹, which is nearly double the conductivity of a single PEDOT:PSS film (3.38 × 10⁻⁴ S m⁻¹).
knowledge_points.evidence: The calculated results show that the conductivity of the PEDOT:PSS/Br-2PACz film is 6.29 × 10⁻⁴ S m⁻¹, which is significantly higher than that of PEDOT:PSS film (3.38 × 10⁻⁴ S m⁻¹).

knowledge_points.content: Deposition of Br-2PACz on PEDOT:PSS washes away a significant portion of the insulating PSS component, reducing the PSS:PEDOT ratio from 7.5:1 to 5:1 and thereby increasing the relative content of conductive PEDOT.
knowledge_points.evidence: The ratio of PSS to PEDOT was calculated to be 7.5:1 and 5:1 for PEDOT:PSS and PEDOT:PSS/Br-2PACz films, respectively, which indicates that a mass of PSS was washed away during the deposition of Br-2PACz.

knowledge_points.content: The work function (WF) of the anode interface increases from 5.03 eV for PEDOT:PSS to 5.18 eV for the PEDOT:PSS/Br-2PACz dual-anode interface, which facilitates more favorable charge transfer.
knowledge_points.evidence: The results indicate that the WF values of PEDOT:PSS, the PEDOT:PSS/Br-2PACz dual-anode interface, and Br-2PACz are 5.03, 5.18, and 5.46 eV, respectively... the higher work function indicates that the HTL is more favorable for charge transfer.

knowledge_points.content: The use of the dual-layer HTL results in a hole mobility (μh) of 2.92 × 10⁻⁴ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ and a more balanced carrier transport ratio (μh/μe) of 0.800 compared to single-layer PEDOT:PSS (μh/μe of 0.384).
knowledge_points.evidence: The data in the table revealed that the μh value of the dual-layer HTL device (2.92 × 10⁻⁴ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹) is significantly higher than that of the single-layer HTL device. Additionally, the μh/μe ratio (0.8) is closer to 1, suggesting a more balanced carrier transmission.

knowledge_points.content: The PEDOT:PSS/Br-2PACz dual-anode interface effectively suppresses charge recombination, as evidenced by a bimolecular recombination coefficient (α) of 0.996, which is closer to unity than the 0.963 observed for PEDOT:PSS.
knowledge_points.evidence: The α values of the devices based on PEDOT:PSS and the dual-anode interface PEDOT:PSS/Br-2PACz are 0.963 and 0.996, respectively. Obviously, the optimal-device α value... is closer to 1, indicating that the second-order recombination generated during charge transfer is negligible.

knowledge_points.content: Devices using the PEDOT:PSS/Br-2PACz dual-anode interface maintain 94.7% of their initial efficiency after 500 hours of storage in a nitrogen environment, compared to only 76.9% for single-layer PEDOT:PSS devices.
knowledge_points.evidence: the device with the PEDOT:PSS/Br-2PACz dual-anode interface still maintains an initial efficiency of 94.7% after 500 h of storage... In contrast, the device based on PEDOT:PSS only maintained an initial efficiency of 76.9%.

knowledge_points.content: The improved stability of the dual-anode interface is attributed to Br-2PACz forming a protective layer that mitigates the acidic corrosion of the ITO electrode by PSS and isolates the active layer from environmental moisture.
knowledge_points.evidence: In addition, Br-2PACz will form a thin film on PEDOT:PSS, which can effectively protect the active layer from the erosion of water in the environment... Br-2PACz can reduce the acid corrosion of ITO by PSS.

knowledge_points.content: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) analysis shows that the surface roughness (RMS) of the PEDOT:PSS/Br-2PACz film is 1.57 nm, which is smoother than single-layer Br-2PACz (2.60 nm) and provides an optimized morphology for carrier transport.
knowledge_points.evidence: The average surface roughness (RMS) of Br-2PACz is about 2.60 nm... The roughness of the PEDOT:PSS/Br-2PACz film is between two monolayer films, about 1.57 nm. The optimized morphology is more conducive to carrier transport.

knowledge_points.content: The dual-anode interface demonstrates broad compatibility by improving the Jsc and FF of OSCs based on other active layer systems, specifically PM6:Y6 and PM6:BTP-eC9.
knowledge_points.evidence: In addition, the PEDOT:PSS/Br-2PACz dual-anode interface was applied to the devices with active layers of PM6:Y6 and PM6:BTP-eC9, respectively... the dual-anode interface can still improve the Jsc and FF of the device.
